subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How do I build a sequence that says something and still works as movement?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of composition: motif, development, repetition, and contrast in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe space, time, weight, and flow as movement qualities using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply dance forms across cultures, treated accurately and respectfully in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving building a longer sequence with structure; correct it and explain why.
Connect refining through self-review and adult feedback with movement as expression, stress relief, and social activity and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Compose, refine, and document a structured movement sequence, then present it to one trusted adult or submit a complete written or notated description instead.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, storyboard, or written description is a full alternative to performing.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
